messages:
rachel: Short thread 1: field customers keep asking for a formal "preserve network" upgrade lane for private deploys. Need a concise policy decision and owners.

troy: Can we scope this as an opt-in installer mode (default unchanged)? i.e., preserve lane vs fast lane. Preserve lane guarantees no CIDR reassign and preserves peer IPs/certs.

anil: Implementation callouts: persist network allocations to an operator-controlled PV or external KV (no TTL), add a `--preserve-network` flag, and run a migration job that reattaches peers after upgrade. Preflight must check reserved ranges for overlap.

joy: UX: console toggle "Preserve customer network (opt-in)" with one-line tradeoffs and an operator approval checkbox. Also provide a small telemetry opt-in to validate peer adjacencies post-upgrade.

rachel: Draft launch criteria: (1) installer accepts reserved_ranges + `--preserve-network`; (2) preflight validation; (3) migration job + retain flag; (4) runbook + rollback steps; (5) 2 pilot validations.

anil: Edge cases: reserved ranges blocking autoscale -> add operator reclaim workflow `redwoodctl network release --confirm` and audit logs (network.reserve/network.release).

troy: Owners: anil -> PR for persistence + preflight (due Fri). joy -> UI copy + telemetry text (due Tue). rachel -> consolidate launch criteria + pilot plan (due Wed).

ops-bot: Pilot slot: 2026-09-01 13:00 UTC. Reply with +1 to claim.

rachel: If pilots show heavy manual steps, ship preserve lane as opt-in alpha and iterate. Otherwise we can gate Private GA on pilot success. Thanks all :thumbsup:
